warnings.description: strip_strategy_annotation_block now calls axc_lexer::tokenize(source) on EVERY compile (every source passes through strip pre-parse), producing a second full tokenization in addition to the parser's own. This is a small, bounded perf cost, NOT a correctness issue — verified tokenize() cannot panic (unknown chars emit a TokenKind::Error token and advance; the loop always terminates on Eof), so a malformed source degrades to 'no Annotation("strategy") token found -> return unchanged', exactly as the old text-find did on non-brace matches, and any real @strategy{...} block still gets its Annotation token emitted because the lexer recovers per-token. Acceptable; noted for the record.

AT-2835's residual-survivor guard checks `line.contains("@strategy {")` (with a space) on non-comment lines. A hypothetical brace-adjacent real block `@strategy{` (no space) that survived stripping would NOT be caught by this residual clause. This is not a live gap: the load-bearing guarantee in AT-2835 is the UNSCOPED `robust == naive_strip_reference` byte-equality over the whole examples/ corpus, and independently verified that every corpus file with a live @strategy block is in fact fully stripped by both algorithms. No corpus file uses the no-space form. The residual clause is a secondary belt-and-suspenders check; its space-sensitivity does not weaken the primary equality proof.

EB.4 NVIDIA re-bless: the GPU-dispatch medians swung ~1.8x-2.4x FASTER vs the prior baseline (e.g. dispatch_saxpy_1m 3219017 -> 1317450 ns; dispatch_vector_add_1m 9941574 -> 5617811; dispatch_handle_saxpy_1m 3169279 -> 1318100), while the CPU-only benches (compile_pipeline, cpu_reference) stayed within a few percent. This is a plausible signature (GPU dispatch got faster under the current driver/clock state; CPU stable), NOT a wrong-bless (a wrong bless shows as a ~100x swing or lost fields, neither present). Direction is safe for the regression gate: a tighter/faster baseline makes the gate STRICTER, it cannot hide a future regression. All 15 entries retain full {group,bench,median_ns,low_ns,high_ns} fields with low<=median<=high. Flagged only so the ~2x GPU delta is on the record as reviewed-and-accepted.

adversarial_probes.strip_utf8_byte_vs_char: PASS - lexer Span is byte-offset based (source stored as &[u8], start/pos are byte positions); at_pos = span.start is byte offset and Rust str slicing is byte-based, so they are consistent. The '@' sigil is ASCII (a valid char boundary), and source[at_pos..].starts_with("@strategy") is asserted. A multibyte char in a preceding comment cannot shift the offset because comments emit no token and the offset is taken from the token span, not a char count.
adversarial_probes.strip_sigil_offset: VERIFIED against the real lexer: next_token captures `start` = position of '@' BEFORE advancing, and lex_annotation returns Span::new(start, self.pos) — span DOES start at '@'. The debug_assert + the saturating_sub(1) fallback are defensive dead-code for a hypothetical future lexer change; primary path is correct. AT-2832 pins the exact byte span (byte-identical removal, verified no off-by-one).

summary: APPROVE. M3.15 is a clean, surgical debt-bundle exactly matching the r3 spec, and it survives the adversarial pass. The highest-risk change (strip_strategy_annotation_block, which runs pre-parse on every compile) is correct: it anchors on the lexer's first Annotation("strategy") token span (comment/string-literal safe), tokenize() has no panic path, byte-offset slicing is UTF-8-safe because the '@' anchor is ASCII and is starts_with-guarded, the '@'-sigil span-start claim is VERIFIED against lex_annotation, and AT-2835 proves byte-identical output to the old algorithm over the whole examples/ corpus (including the subtle matmul_f32_tiled.axc line-10-decoy short-circuit that keeps the equality green). EB.3 spawns via arg-vector (no shell-injection surface) with child-only env overrides and carries the nested-cargo self-deadlock note in both clap help and the handler. EB.4's two-key baseline is well-formed (15 full-field entries per machine, schema v2, round-trips), AT-2837 is green-this-cycle and not weakened; the ~2x-faster GPU-dispatch medians are a plausible driver/clock delta (CPU benches stable), gate-safe (tighter baseline = stricter), not a wrong-bless. The empty-kernel golden is byte-identical to what the current tree emits (independently regenerated + cmp'd) and its failure message names both the regen command and the legitimate re-bless cause. The frozen-value refresh changed ONLY numeric literals, no tolerance smuggled. CHANGELOG spot-checks (M3.6/M3.13/M4.1) are all corroborated by git log — the one apparent discrepancy (M4.1 'Phases 1-4' vs the stale MEMORY.md 'Phase 1 only') is resolved in the CHANGELOG's favor by the real Phase-2/3/4 merge commits. AT-2840 is non-vacuous (lvp_icd.json is not a substring of lvp_icd.x86_64.json). Three informational warnings recorded (double-tokenize perf, residual-clause space-sensitivity, the reviewed ~2x GPU-median swing); none block merge. Scope discipline confirmed: zero touches to lexer/parser/hir/mir/codegen crates, examples/*.axc, ci.yml, or the axc-runtime ICD doc-comments.
